name: Max Engling
gradeNote: Strong conservative answers on the iVoterGuide questionnaire on life, marriage, religious conscience, voter ID and voter-roll maintenance, but he has no voting or official record, and his Second Amendment and fiscal answers are general rather than specific.
description: Former U.S. House Republican staffer and regional director for Sen. Jim Banks who defeated incumbent Diego Morales for the Republican nomination at the June 2026 convention.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception and that abortion providers should not receive taxpayer funds; questionnaire only, no voting record.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly agreed that marriage is one man and one woman, that parents have a fundamental right to direct their children's health and education, and that transitioning a child is child abuse.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their religious beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Answered the gun-restrictions question only by quoting the U.S. and Indiana constitutions, without stating a specific position; not rated by NRA-PVF (which grades only federal and legislative races).
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly opposes voting without photo ID, says he is cleaning ineligible voters from the rolls, opposes sanctuary cities and agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Proposes competitive bidding, streamlined IT and lower mailing costs for the office; no tax, spending-record or scorecard evidence found.

name: Lauri A. Shillings
gradeNote: Not rated: her campaign site addresses only office administration (secure and transparent elections, simpler business filings, cutting red tape, office independence), and she did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire, so there is no position on five of the six values.
description: Chair of the Hamilton County Libertarian Party and creative director at the University of Indianapolis, running as the Libertarian nominee.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No position found; did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No position found on marriage, parental rights or gender issues.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found on religious liberty.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found on the Second Amendment.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Campaign site mentions cutting red tape and secure, transparent elections, but states no position on voter ID, school choice or other limited-government issues.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: No position found on taxes or spending.

name: Greg Ballard
gradeNote: As Indianapolis mayor he publicly opposed Indiana's 2015 Religious Freedom Restoration Act and urged adding sexual orientation and gender identity to state civil-rights law, and in 2014 he proposed a 43% increase in the city's public-safety income tax; no public positions on abortion or guns were found.
description: Former two-term Republican mayor of Indianapolis (2008-2015) and retired Marine lieutenant colonel, running as an independent on the Lincoln Party line.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No position found; he did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire on abortion.
gradeJustifications.marriage: In 2015 urged lawmakers to add sexual orientation and gender identity to state anti-discrimination law.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Publicly denounced Indiana's 2015 Religious Freedom Restoration Act and asked that city ordinances be exempted from it.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found; he did not answer the iVoterGuide gun question and is not rated by NRA-PVF in this race.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Campaigns on independent redistricting commissions, open primaries and a nonpartisan voter guide; did not answer the iVoterGuide photo-ID question.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: As mayor proposed raising Indianapolis's public-safety income tax from 0.35% to 0.5% (approved 19-10 in 2014) to fund more police officers.

name: Elise Nieshalla
gradeNote: In office she voted for a non-ESG investment policy for the state's Hoosier START retirement plan and chairs a state financial officers' national-debt task force; on the iVoterGuide questionnaire she gave consistently conservative answers on life, marriage, religious conscience, constitutional carry, parental rights and voter ID.
description: Incumbent Republican comptroller appointed in 2023, former Boone County Council president and former Indiana Department of Commerce economic development manager.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception, supports making abortion illegal with life-saving care for mother and child, and opposes taxpayer funds for abortion providers.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly agreed that marriage is one man and one woman, that parents direct their children's health and education, and that transitioning a child is child abuse.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their religious beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Supports Indiana's constitutional carry law, with carry restrictions limited to groups such as felons, domestic abusers and the adjudicated mentally incompetent.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and strongly opposes voting without photo ID and sanctuary cities.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Voted in March 2025 for a non-ESG policy for a public retirement savings plan, chairs a national-debt task force with 37 state financial officers, and runs the state transparency portal and a federal-spending dashboard.

name: John Schick
gradeNote: Not rated: his public statements cover only the comptroller's office (independence from the governing party and a more detailed spending-transparency portal); he did not answer the 2026 surveys, and no positions on the other values were found.
description: Chesterton business consultant and former Libertarian Party state treasurer, running his third or fourth campaign for comptroller/auditor.

gradeJustifications.proLife: No position found; did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire.
gradeJustifications.marriage: No position found on marriage, parental rights or gender issues.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No position found on religious liberty.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: No position found on the Second Amendment.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: No position found beyond saying the comptroller should be independent of the governor and legislature.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Says he would rework the state transparency portal so it shows how money is spent, but states no tax or spending-level position.

name: Daniel Elliott
gradeNote: As treasurer he put BlackRock on an ESG watchlist in 2024 and, as an INPRS board member, voted to replace it as manager of a roughly $969 million portfolio; on the iVoterGuide questionnaire he gave consistently conservative answers on life, marriage, religious conscience, guns (no new restrictions), parental rights and voter ID.
description: Incumbent Republican state treasurer first elected in 2022, former Morgan County Council member and software engineer/consultant.

gradeJustifications.proLife: Would allow abortion only when the mother's life is in imminent danger, strongly agreed that life deserves protection from conception, and opposes taxpayer funds for abortion providers.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Strongly agreed that marriage is one man and one woman, that parents direct their children's health and education, and that transitioning a child is child abuse.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Strongly disagreed that individuals and businesses should be required to provide services that violate their religious beliefs.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Answered that no gun restrictions are needed because the constitution protects the right to keep and bear arms.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Strongly agreed with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and strongly opposes voting without photo ID and sanctuary cities; opposes minimum-wage laws.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Placed BlackRock on an ESG watchlist, voted to replace it on a state pension portfolio, and co-founded a 37-member state financial officers' coalition on the national debt.

name: Rudy Yakym
gradeNote: Strong on life, marriage and guns (SBA Pro-Life America A+, NRA-PVF A+ and endorsed), but his fiscal and limited-government scores are good rather than top-tier: Heritage Action 85% in the 119th Congress and Club for Growth 95% for 2025 with a 78% lifetime score.
description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 2nd District since 2022, campaigning on limited government, lower taxes and reduced regulation.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023 and 2025.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: No specific religious-liberty vote, cosponsorship or statement found beyond his vote against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A+ and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action score of 85% in the 119th Congress; campaign pledges to cut regulations and restore federal-state balance.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 95% but lifetime 78% (below its Defender threshold); Heritage Action 85%.

name: Marlin A. Stutzman
gradeNote: Consistently top-rated: SBA Pro-Life America A+, NRA-PVF A and endorsed, Heritage Action 100% and Club for Growth 100% for 2025 (94% lifetime, ranked first); he cosponsored religious-liberty bills in his earlier House tenure and voted for a state marriage amendment in 2005.
description: Howe farmer and business owner, former Indiana House and Senate member, who returned to Congress in 2024 after previously holding the seat.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act and, as a state representative in 2005, for Indiana's one-man-one-woman marriage amendment.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Cosponsored the Marriage and Religious Freedom Act (H.R. 3133, 2013) and signed on to the First Amendment Defense Act (H.R. 2802, 2015).
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action 100% in the 119th Congress; campaign calls for finishing the border wall and says education is not a federal issue.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 100% (lifetime 94%, Defender of Economic Freedom); says he authored the Conservative Congressional budget.

name: Jim Baird
gradeNote: Strong on life, marriage, religious liberty and guns (SBA A+, NRA-PVF A and endorsed, votes against the Equality Act and Respect for Marriage Act), but fiscal and limited-government scores are lower: Heritage Action 84% and Club for Growth 90% for 2025 with a 77% lifetime score.
description: Farmer, small-business owner and Vietnam veteran seeking a fifth term; former Putnam County commissioner and Indiana state representative.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023 and 2025.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Voted against the 2021 Equality Act (H.R. 5) and the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action score of 84% in the 119th Congress.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 90% but lifetime 77% (below its Defender threshold); Heritage Action 84%.

name: Victoria Spartz
gradeNote: Consistently A across values: SBA Pro-Life America A+, NRA-PVF A and endorsed, Heritage Action 92%, and Club for Growth 95% for 2025 (91% lifetime, Defender of Economic Freedom); she voted against the Equality Act and Respect for Marriage Act and against the September 2025 stopgap spending bill.
description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 5th District since 2021 and won a third term in 2024.

gradeJustifications.proLife: SBA Pro-Life America A+; voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act in 2023 and 2025.
gradeJustifications.marriage: Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
gradeJustifications.religiousLiberty: Voted against the 2021 Equality Act (H.R. 5) and the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.
gradeJustifications.secondAmendment: Rated A and endorsed by NRA-PVF for 2026.
gradeJustifications.limitedGov: Heritage Action score of 92% in the 119th Congress.
gradeJustifications.fiscal: Club for Growth 2025 score 95% (lifetime 91%, Defender of Economic Freedom); one of two Republicans to vote against the September 2025 stopgap spending bill.
